chunks: Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Razzaz from Muhammad ibn Isa from Ali ibn Sulayman said:

I wrote to him, meaning Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him): 'May I be sacrificed for you! I have no child, and I have lands (diya') which I inherited from my father, and some of which I acquired. I do not fear the unexpected events. If I have no child and an event befalls me, what do you think, may I be sacrificed for you, that I dedicate some of it upon the poor of my brothers and the weak, or sell it and give in charity with its price during my lifetime for them? For I fear that the endowment will not be enforced after my death. So if I endow it during my lifetime, is it for me to eat from it during the days of my life, or not?'}},
    {

So he (peace be upon him) wrote: 'I understood your letter regarding your lands. And it is not for you to eat from it from the charity, for if you eat from it, it will not be enforced if you have heirs. So sell it and give in charity with some of its price during your lifetime. And if you give in charity, withhold for yourself what sustains you, similar to what the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) did.'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: The Commander of the Faithful, a title referring to Imam Ali (AS).
key_terms.الْوَقْفُ: Endowment, a charitable trust where the asset is dedicated for religious or charitable purposes.
key_terms.ضِيَاعٌ: Lands or estates, specifically agricultural lands or properties.
key_terms.يَنْفُذُ: To be enforced or valid, particularly in the context of legal rulings or endowments.

ai.seo_question: Can an endower consume the produce of their waqf while alive?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies the distinction between *waqf* (endowment) and *sadaqah* (charity) regarding lifetime consumption, ruling that a donor cannot eat from the principal of an endowment if he has heirs, as it invalidates the gift. He advises selling the property to give the proceeds in charity while retaining a portion for personal sustenance, citing the precedent of Imam Ali (AS) to emphasize the importance of preserving the charitable corpus for the poor. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the permanence of endowments and the specific conditions under which a donor may benefit from their own charity.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Ja’fa Al Razaz, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ali Bin Suleyman who said,

‘I wrote to him<sup>asws</sup>, meaning Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! There is no child for me, and for me is a place which I inherited from my father, and some which I profited, and I am not secure from the adversities. Since there is no child for me, and an adversity occurs with me, so what is your<sup>asws</sup> view, may I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>, shall I dedicate some of it upon the poor brethren of mine and the weak ones, or shall I sell it and give in charity to them with its price during my lifetime, as I fear that the dedication would not be enforced after my death. So if I were to dedicate it during my lifetime, so it would be for me that I would be eating from it during the days of my life, or not?’

So he<sup>asws</sup> wrote: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> understood your letter in the matter of your place, and it is not for you that you eat from it from the charity, for if you were to eat from it, the inheritance of yours would not be enforced, therefore sell and give in charity with some of its price during your lifetime, and if you were to give in charity, withhold some of it for yourself what is your livelihood, similar to what Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> did’.
en.sarwar: 33. Muhammad ibn Ja‘far al-Raziy has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Ali ibn Sulayman who has narrated the following: “

I once wrote to him (the Imam), abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ‘I pray to Allah to keep my soul in service for your cause, I do not have any children and I have assets that I inherited from my father and myself earned a certain amount, but I do not feel safe from something happening. If something happens to me and I have no children, what do you think I must do, I pray to Allah to keep my soul in service for your cause? Can I make a certain amount of it an endowment for the needy, of the oppressed brothers (in belief) or sell it and spend upon them in my lifetime? I fear that endowment may not be managed properly after I die and if I make an endowment for my own survival will I be able to eat thereof?’

He (the Imam), ‘Alayhi al-Salam, wrote, ‘I understood your letter in the matter of your assets. You cannot eat from charity (endowment), if so the law of endowment is not followed just as if you had heirs. You can sell and give as charity a certain amount of the proceeds in your lifetime. If you give as charity you can keep for yourself for your sustenance just as ’Amir al-Mu’minin had done.’”
